_about.title: Hurricane Rafael canon timeline
_about.purpose: Machine-readable truth for every data-stream generator and validator. If a stream, a story or a design note disagrees with this file, this file wins. It applies 00_scenario/canon_decisions.md.
structure: Top-level keys are topics (storm, alerts, port, spill, power, utility_cyber, water, health, calls_911, sar, closures, military_aviation, relief, drones, dark_vessel, gps_interference, channel_attack, fraud_and_contracts, influence_operation, insurance, aid, investigation_and_attribution, broadcast).

A time is an object with utc (ISO, minute precision), local (ISO with offset), day (local calendar day offset from landfall day) and a label. A day-only item has day, date_local, weekday and time=null: the sources give no time of day and a generator may pick one inside that local day.
A window is {start, end}; end=null means open-ended in the sources.
sources lists the MSEL event ids (EVT-, GW-EVT-) and public facts (PUB-, GW-PUB-) each item comes from.

public_from_day is the first local day a participant-readable stream (news, social posts, press releases, alerts) may show the item; null means never public. Sensor-type streams (AIS, telemetry, logs, health data) carry the truth from when it happens, without labels that explain it.
value=null with a note means the sources give no number. Generators must not invent a headline number; pick plausible detail only where the note says they may.

conventions.msel_time_convention: An MSEL label such as 'D+7 14:30Z' means 14:30 UTC on the UTC calendar date D0+7 days. Because Corpus Christi is 5 or 6 hours behind UTC, events before 05:00Z fall on the previous local day.
